evals.name: single-coherent-feature
evals.prompt: I added session refresh logic to my auth module plus a test for it, can you commit this for me? repo is at <REPO_PATH>
evals.expected_output: One Conventional Commits-style commit (likely feat(auth|session): ...), header ~50 chars, wrapped body explaining why, drafted and shown for approval before running git add/git commit, then actually committed via git commit -F with a temp file.

evals.name: mixed-unrelated-changes-split
evals.prompt: commit my changes, repo is at <REPO_PATH>
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the diff mixes a bug fix (calculator.py divide-by-zero guard), an unrelated doc formatting cleanup (README.md), and an unrelated new utility script (scripts/format_currency.py). Splits into separate commits (e.g. fix(calculator): ..., docs: ..., feat/chore(scripts): ...) each staged and committed independently, with developer approval shown before committing.

evals.name: breaking-api-change
evals.prompt: I renamed and changed the signature of get_user_v1 to get_user in api.py, removing the old function entirely. can you write a proper commit message and commit it? repo is at <REPO_PATH>
evals.expected_output: Header uses `!` (e.g. feat(api)!: ... or refactor(api)!: ...) and includes a BREAKING CHANGE: footer explaining what broke and how to migrate. Message shown for approval before staging/committing.
